evidence.detail: Detached checkout HEAD exactly matches the launcher-supplied target SHA; the base-to-target diff was available and contained no uncommitted changes.
The diff modifies the six implementation paths allowed by ISSUE-0017 plus its authorized decision, issue, handoff, prior-review, roadmap, and current-status records.

The round-1 implementation now requires persistentBrowser.enabled to be exactly true and mode to be exactly "never"; its regression test covers an explicitly disabled control carrying stale mode "never".
Focused analyzer and graph tests completed successfully: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_graph tests.test_analyzer` ran 49 tests with exit 0.
The complete required test command ran 206 tests but exited 1 with 76 server-test errors because the review sandbox denied loopback socket binding.
The required compile command exited 1 because the read-only sandbox denied creation of `__pycache__`.
Governance validation exited 1 because no writable temporary directory was available to its launcher smoke tests.

evidence: Expected: all three required checks must execute successfully against the exact candidate before an issue review can pass.

Observed: the full suite exited 1 with 76 PermissionError failures when server tests attempted loopback binds; compile exited 1 when bytecode output was denied; governance validation exited 1 because no usable temporary directory existed.

The committed handoff reports locally obtained passing results—206 tests, compile exit 0, and governance validation passing—but repository rules require independent verification and explicitly treat author claims as non-authoritative.
findings.remediation: Rerun the exact required commands against target commit 72910d8b22dd74d664036d74c0d909e1d6a32c6a in an approved environment that permits bytecode/temp-file creation and loopback socket binding, then supply the real commit-bound output to a fresh review. If the known sandbox limitation is instead accepted, that requires an explicit human decision; the reviewer cannot infer acceptance.
findings.title: Required verification cannot be independently completed in the review sandbox
findings.verification: Confirm exit 0 from `python3 -m py_compile $(git ls-files '*.py')`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` with all 206 tests passing, and `python3 scripts/validate_repo.py` against the exact target SHA.

evidence: Expected: committed issue and handoff records accurately identify the current round and its evidence.
Observed: the issue header still says `Candidate SHA: round 0 is this commit`, although the reviewed target is explicitly the round-1 repair.

Observed: the handoff's primary implementation summary still describes qualification as requiring only `persistentBrowser.mode == "never"`, and its main acceptance/check tables still report 205 tests; the later round-1 appendix correctly adds the enabled requirement and reports 206 tests. These internally contradictory records make the current candidate evidence stale even though the appendix describes the repair.
findings.remediation: Update the issue candidate identity and the handoff's primary outcome, changed-files description, acceptance mapping, and verification table so they consistently describe round 1: persistentBrowser.enabled must be true, the candidate is the round-1 commit, and the suite contains 206 tests. Preserve prior-round results only in clearly labeled history.
findings.title: Issue and handoff records remain partly stale after the round-1 repair
findings.verification: Inspect the repaired records and confirm every current-candidate summary agrees with the round-1 appendix, source, test count, and exact target SHA; then run governance validation and obtain a fresh review because the documentation change creates a new candidate.

limitations: The read-only review environment cannot create bytecode or temporary directories and cannot bind loopback sockets, so the required compile, governance, and complete test checks could not succeed independently.
No live-tenant authentication or Microsoft Graph call was performed; ISSUE-0017 does not require one and introduces no new endpoint or permission.
The checkout presents the target as a detached, shallow/grafted commit, but both supplied commit objects and the exact base-to-target diff were available and matched the launcher identities.
review.summary: The round-1 code repair is correct under source inspection and all 49 focused graph/analyzer tests pass, including the disabled persistent-browser regression. The review is nevertheless BLOCKED because the three mandatory checks could not all execute successfully in this sandbox and the committed issue/handoff records contain stale round-0 descriptions and test counts. Residual risk is limited to the unverified full-suite/governance/compile evidence and the documented lack of live-tenant validation; no additional product-code defect was identified.
